lines.text: For over one thousand years, these colossal stone walls were invincibleâ€”until one morning in 1453.
Sultan Mehmed the Second unleashed the greatest super-weapon of the Middle Ages: a bronze cannon firing twelve-hundred-pound boulders.
When Roman chains blocked the harbor, seventy Ottoman warships were dragged entirely overland on greased logs.
On May twenty-ninth, thousands of elite Janissaries stormed the fractured Saint Romanus gate.
Refusing to flee, Emperor Constantine the Eleventh tore off his imperial insignia and charged into the breach.
The Roman Empire finally fell where its last emperor stood. Subscribe to Beyond History for more epic battles.
